title: Recommendation Hub & Policy Composer for Batching + Cache — explainers, cost-quality slider, and guardrail states
creator: Dana Kato
description: Design a Recommendation Hub and Policy Composer inside the Redwood Console that makes batching and cache configuration actionable and explainable for engineers. The feature surfaces per-route recommendations, an interactive cost-quality slider, preflight guardrails (hard limits + soft warnings), and a lightweight what-if simulator so users can preview latency and cost changes before applying. The goal is to reduce incorrect manual tuning, lower average token cost across typical workloads, and provide clear rationale for automated suggestions so platform teams can adopt recommendations with confidence.
acceptance_criteria: High-fidelity screens for Hub list, detail panel, and composer modal are in Figma and linked
Interactive prototype demonstrates slider, guardrail states (ok/warning/blocked), and what-if simulation steps
Copy includes short explainers for batching, prefix cache, kv-cache reuse, and quantization interaction
Telemetry events defined for accept/decline recommendation, simulation runs, and applied changes (links to GH issue)
Design handoff includes tokens, spacing, and accessible tooltip content; engineers have a component spec and edge-case notes
notes: Trade-off: expose enough knobs for power users (max batch, max latency SLO) but hide complexity behind 'advanced' toggles
Decision log: prefer inline cost delta estimates over absolute cost projections to avoid false precision
Constraint: backend needs per-route latency profile (ENG-2012) to power realistic simulations — blocked until ENG-2012 test data is available
Accessibility: color alone must not indicate guardrail state; use icons and text labels
Metrics: recommend a per-route baseline and expected P95 delta; include confidence bucket (high/medium/low) based on sample size
